Querying `system.functions` for `arrayLastIndex` therefore still yields empty documentation/version metadata, and both updated reference files continue listing it as undocumented.

2. **`src/Functions/array/arrayAggregation.cpp:499`** — The advertised syntax for `arraySum` names `arrayMax`. A client generating `arraySum([1,2,3,4])` from this metadata instead executes `arrayMax([1,2,3,4])`, returning `4` rather than `10`.

3. **`src/Functions/array/arrayFirstLast.cpp:254`** — `arrayLast` is documented with a nonexistent `λ=func(...)` argument. Following it with `arrayLast(λ = (x -> x > 0), [-1,2])` produces a parsing/name-resolution error instead of returning `2`.

4. **`src/Functions/array/arrayAll.cpp:70`** — The syntax incorrectly makes the lambda mandatory. `arrayAll([1,1])` is a supported identity-overload and returns `1`, but the published metadata says no such call exists. The implementation explicitly supports `f(array)` as `f(x -> x, array)` in the [function contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/master/src/Functions/array/arrayAll.h).

5. **`src/Functions/array/arrayExists.cpp:71`** — The syntax likewise omits the supported no-lambda overload. `arrayExists([0,1])` returns `1`, while the metadata represents it as an invalid signature. This overload is documented in the [function contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/master/src/Functions/array/arrayExists.h).

6. **`src/Functions/array/arrayAggregation.cpp:483`** — The `arrayMax` returned-value metadata says a lambda call returns the minimum lambda result. For the included input `[4,8,12,16]` and `[1,2,1,2]`, the text predicts `4`, while `arrayMax` returns `12`.

7. **`src/Functions/array/arrayFirstLast.cpp:265`** — The `arrayLast` “No match” example invokes `arrayFirst`. With distinguishing inputs such as `[1,2,3]` and `[1,0,3]`, adapting that example returns `1`; the documented function should return the last matching value, `3`.

8. **`src/Functions/array/arraySplit.cpp:137`** — The lambda for `arrayReverseSplit` is labeled optional even though this implementation requires an expression. Following the argument documentation with `arrayReverseSplit([1,2,3])` is rejected instead of returning a split array.

9. **`src/Functions/array/arrayAggregation.cpp:510`** — `arraySum` is assigned introduction version `21.1`, although it already existed in 20.x; it was explicitly identified as existing before the 21.1 additions ([ClickHouse issue #17849](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/17849)). Compatibility tooling targeting 20.x will therefore suppress `arraySum` even though `SELECT arraySum([1,2])` works there.

3. arrayFirstLast.cpp `examples_last` "No match" — runs arrayFirst not arrayLast.

## Defects

**1. `src/Functions/array/arrayAggregation.cpp` (~line 497) — `syntax_sum` declares the wrong function name.**
`FunctionDocumentation::Syntax syntax_sum = "arrayMax([func(x[, y1, ..., yN])], source[, cond1, ... , condN])";` — the syntax string for **arraySum** literally says `arrayMax`. Concrete failure: the rendered docs page for `arraySum` shows `arrayMax(...)` as its call syntax; a reader copying it calls `arrayMax` and gets a max, or a "no such overload" error, never the documented sum. (Contrast with the surrounding `syntax_min/syntax_max/syntax_avg/syntax_prod`, which all use their own names — a clear copy-paste slip.)

**2. `src/Functions/array/arrayAggregation.cpp` (~line 481) — `returned_value_max` states the wrong result semantics.**
`returned_value_max = "Returns the maximum element ..., or the minimum element of the lambda results if provided."` — for **arrayMax** it says "minimum". Concrete failure: a reader is told `arrayMax(lambda, ...)` returns the *minimum* of the lambda results, which is exactly backwards; and it directly contradicts the diff's own `examples_max` ("..."/"12"), which returns the true maximum. The doc text and its example disagree.

**3. `src/Functions/array/arrayFirstLast.cpp` (~line 250) — the `arrayLast` "No match" example executes `arrayFirst`, not `arrayLast`.**
Inside the `documentation_last` block the "No match" entry runs `SELECT arrayFirst(x, y -> x=y, [0, 1, 2], [3, 3, 3]) ...`. Concrete failure: the example labeled as demonstrating `arrayLast`'s no-match behavior actually invokes `arrayFirst`; a user following the example sees `arrayFirst`'s behavior, and the documented `arrayLast` no-match path is never shown. (The sibling `arrayLastOrNull` "No match" example correctly uses `arrayLastOrNull`.)

**4. `src/Functions/array/arrayFirstLastIndex.cpp` (end of hunk, ~line 168) — documentation is built for `arrayLastIndex` but never registered, while it is removed from both test-reference exemption lists.**
The added code constructs `description_last / syntax_last / ... / documentation_last`, but the surviving registration line is `factory.registerFunction<FunctionArrayLastIndex>();` — it does **not** pass `documentation_last`. So `arrayLastIndex` still has no documentation and no version information at runtime, yet the PR removes `arrayLastIndex` from both `tests/.../02415_all_new_functions_must_be_documented.reference` and `...must_have_version_information.reference`. Concrete failure: the "new functions must be documented" / "must have version information" tests will now fail, because `arrayLastIndex` is still undocumented/unversioned but is no longer on the exemption allowlist — the very thing those two reference edits are protecting against. (Every other function in this diff that was removed from the lists gets a documentation block wired into its `registerFunction` call; `arrayLastIndex`'s block is dead code.)

**5. `src/Functions/array/arraySplit.cpp` (~line 128) — `arrayReverseSplit` marks its lambda argument "Optional." when it is mandatory.**
In `arguments_split`, the first entry is `{"func(x[, y1, ..., yN])", "Optional. A lambda function ..."}`. Unlike `arrayMin/Max/Sum/Avg/Prod` (whose `func` genuinely is optional), `arraySplit`/`arrayReverseSplit` have no no-lambda overload, so the predicate is required — and the matching `arraySplit` `arguments` entry correctly does *not* say "Optional." Concrete failure: a user reads that the lambda is optional for `arrayReverseSplit`, calls `arrayReverseSplit(source)` without a lambda, and gets a syntax/arity error that the docs said shouldn't happen.
